tasks.title: Thin-Film Optics & Polarization Shift
tasks.objective: Connect Brewster’s angle, p-polarised reflectance and colour-contrast changes.
steps: Load the prepared WAVE setup: n₀ = 1.00, n₁ = 1.33, n₂ = 1.50 and p-polarisation.
Sweep the incidence angle from 0° to 80° while watching first-boundary reflectance.
Return to θB ≈ 53.1° and record what happens to reflected saturation and contrast.
Explain why p-polarised reflection approaches zero at the boundary.

tasks.title: Filament Thermal Dynamics & Inrush Analysis
tasks.objective: Explain why a cold filament draws a larger current than a hot operating filament.
steps: Load the prepared series circuit; S1 begins open and L1 begins cool.
Allow the lamp to remain cool, then close S1 to capture the current peak.
Compare peak current with the later steady lamp current.
Use R(T) = R₀(1 + αΔT) to explain the difference.

tasks.title: 3-Mark Guided Circuit Fault Diagnostic
tasks.objective: Use independent meter evidence to identify and classify a hidden circuit fault.
steps: Load a random hidden fault in challenge mode.
Record at least two purposeful readings, ideally using more than one meter mode or location.
Select the faulty area and classify the fault.
Submit the diagnosis and use the feedback to improve the evidence pathway.

tasks.title: Wheatstone Bridge Balance Extension
tasks.objective: Relate resistance ratios to a near-zero detector current in a balanced bridge.
steps: Load the balanced Wheatstone bridge and inspect the detector branch.
Change one arm resistance, observe imbalance, then restore balance.
Explain why matching resistance ratios produce no detector current.
